basis: 10 rows/s: widefeed1 ticks twice a second for 5 pairs; ~220 bytes a row with two 11-level vectors. One pair for an hour is 7200 rows (~1.6MB); the sym filter keeps a request to one pair's rows
A day of one pair is 172800 rows (~38MB): enough to rebuild a session's book offline
2 rows/s: one fill a second scored at 2 horizons; ~56 bytes a row. A day raw is 172800 rows; a week is 1.2M; so a raw week stops at the row limit and is for aggregates

~3.5 rows/s from cryptomock1: each fill scored at 2 horizons; ~80 bytes a row. A day raw is ~300k rows, past the row limit, so a raw request is for a recent window - an outside subscriber's snapshot (#984) asks for the last minutes - and a day is for aggregates
200 to 1000 deals a day (scripts/dev/make_fx_deals_duckdb.py): a month is at most 31000 rows

at most the market_data rate for one pair, written only on a change: the demo feeds give a pair about 4 books a second (quote and fx_orderbook, twice a second each), so an hour is ~14400 rows at ~80 bytes (~1.2MB); the sym filter keeps a request to one pair, and the current price is its last row
A day of one pair at the demo rate is ~345600 rows (~28MB): enough to replay a session's price path offline
